modules.title: 1. River of ice
modules.activity: Cinematic flyover up Muir Inlet (S1); how glaciers flow and how a terminus advances or retreats.

facts.text: In 1941 Muir Glacier was a large tidewater calving valley glacier, with Riggs Glacier as a tributary.
Muir Glacier had been retreating since the mid-eighteenth century.

facts.text: The advance or retreat of a glacier reflects many factors: snowfall rate, topography and climate trends; tidewater glaciers are even more complicated.
Seawater undermines tidewater ice fronts and large blocks calve off.
The Little Ice Age advance here reached its maximum about 1750, when general melting began.
